title: Harbour
suits: logistics, shipping, supply chain, travel, climate and ocean products, marketplaces that move goods; pitches that want openness and steady work. Walk data-tod from dawn to night across the deck.

params.data-tod: 0 dawn · .25 morning · .5 bright day · .75 golden hour · 1 night (lighthouse sweeping, buoys blinking)
params.--brand: on the section: one sail, the lighthouse stripes, the ferry's band and funnel, the box the crane is lifting, the fishing boat's stripe, the ship's funnel
params.--brand-2: on the section: the gantry cranes, a second sail, the dinghy
params.--field (set by the scene): the sky behind the headline zone, so --ink-auto stays right

details: a gantry crane lifts a box off the docked ship, trolleys it ashore, sets it on the stack and goes back for the next (36 s); the box sways a little on its cables while it travels
the box the crane carries is the brand colour; once set down, the spreader comes back empty
the ship's bridge windows and the quay lamps come on as the light drops; red aircraft lights blink on the crane apexes
once the light drops, the lighthouse beam sweeps every 12 s, long when side-on, and flashes when it turns to face you
a red buoy blinks every 4 s and a green one every 3 s after dark, each bobbing and leaning on its own beat
three sailboats bob and heel out of phase; one sail is the brand colour, one the second brand colour
a ferry crosses right to left every 80 s with a bow wave, a wake, smoke from its funnel and, at night, lit decks and a red sidelight
a fishing boat in the foreground rocks slower and heavier than the dinghy; its mast lamp comes on after dark
the dinghy tugs at its rope on the pier bollard
a gull on the end of the pier turns its head every few seconds
gulls glide in wide loops over the port and flap only now and then; white against the day sky, dark against dawn and dusk
water laps at the pier piles
swell: three bands of wave crests slide and breathe, each on its own beat
glints sparkle in a path under the sun (and under the moon at night); elsewhere they drift slowly
the sun rises low on the right, stands high at midday and sets at the far right; a thin crescent and stars at night
the pier lamp lights a pool and a long reflection at night
fair-weather cumulus at midday, long lit streaks at dawn and dusk; the clouds drift with the breeze
the headland's cottages light up at dusk
